title: Introduce resilient retry-composer and ergonomic stream-adapter bridge across SDK languages
author: Samira Cortez
release_notes: Added RetryComposer and StreamAdapterBridge to Python/TS/Go SDKs; bumped patch versions. No behavioral breaking changes expected; opt-in APIs for advanced retry compositions.
description:
Context and goal: Customer signals and internal telemetry showed several flaky streaming consumers when transient auth errors coincided with aggressive retry windows. This PR introduces a cross-language design: RetryComposer (policy combinator for backoff/decider composition) and StreamAdapterBridge (lightweight ergonomic adapter that exposes cancelable async iterables and buffered push/pull views) so application code can express layered retry strategies without duplicating language-specific plumbing.

What this PR does (single-line description followed by details): Adds a library-level retry composer and a small adapter layer implemented in each SDK. The composer lets teams combine built-in presets (standard, conservative, aggressive) with custom predicates and credential-aware backoffs. The adapter normalizes streaming primitives so higher-level consumers (console tooling, middleware, and integrations) can reuse the same semantics across Python/TS/Go.

Checklist: [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4821) [x] Unit tests for all SDKs [x] End-to-end smoke test on hosted staging [x] Docs snippets and migration note [x] Version bumps for py/ts/go packages [ ] Follow-up telemetry gating (ENG-4837)

Implementation summary: - Core design is language-agnostic: RetryComposer exposes compose(presets..., customPredicate) => policy. Policies implement shouldRetry(err, attemptMeta) and nextDelayMs(attemptMeta). - StreamAdapterBridge wraps underlying transport iterators/streams and provides: pause/resume, graceful drain on cancel, token-aware retry hooks, and a small heartbeat jitter to avoid stampedes. - Python: added retry_composer.py and stream_adapter/bridge.py under redwood_sdk/experimental; tiny public shim at redwood.client.streams.RetryBridge for opt-in use. Tests and docstrings included. - TypeScript: new package subfolder packages/sdk-streams with retryComposer.ts and adapterBridge.ts; exports added to index. Examples updated in examples/streams. - Go: added retrycomposer package and streambridge.go with context-aware cancellation semantics; added examples in examples/streaming. - Documentation: docs/sdk/retry-composer.md and docs/sdk/stream-adapter.md with examples for 3 languages and recommended presets. Migration note included in CHANGELOG.

Commits (high level): * 8f2a0c6 - initial multi-language design and interface contracts (design doc link) * c3d5b4a - python: implementation, tests, docs * 7b9e21f - typescript: implementation, tests, examples, build fix * e1d2f7b - go: implementation, examples, go mod tidy, linter fixes * a9c4d12 - cross-sdk integration tests and staging smoke harness * 5d4f001 - docs and CHANGELOG, bump package versions

Files/areas touched (high level): - sdks/python/redwood_sdk/experimental/retry_composer.py - sdks/python/redwood_sdk/experimental/stream_adapter/bridge.py - sdks/python/tests/test_retry_composer.py - packages/sdk-streams/src/retryComposer.ts - packages/sdk-streams/src/adapterBridge.ts - packages/sdk-typescript/src/index.ts (exports) - go/sdk/retrycomposer/* - go/sdk/streambridge/streambridge.go - docs/sdk/retry-composer.md - docs/sdk/stream-adapter.md - examples/streams/* - ci/workflows/smoke-staging.yml (added a job)

Design notes and tradeoffs: The composer intentionally does not change default SDK behavior; it's opt-in. We chose an explicit compositional API rather than autowiring to preserve predictable SLOs. The adapter adds a slight handshake on stream initiation to attach token-tied hooks — this cost was measured at ~0.2ms/handshake in staging and considered acceptable given reduced retries and overall better tail latency.

Review thread highlights: - Daniel Hughes: "Can we make the python API match the TS shape more closely? The current shim renames next_delay -> nextDelay in TS which is confusing." (requested change) - Author (Samira): "Changed Python shim to provide a camelCase surface on the opt-in bridge and kept snake_case internal helpers; updated tests to assert both naming docstrings." - Marta Ivanova: "Please add an integration test that simulates token refresh mid-stream and asserts no duplicate events." (requested change) - Author: "Added go/python/ts integration tests that run a mock auth server and assert at-most-once consumer semantics; test added in e1d2f7b and CI updated." - Kenji Sato: "Lint and vet fixes in Go were required; confirm no goroutine leaks." (resolved) - Author: "Run with `-race` in CI smoke-stage job; fixed one leak in streambridge draining logic and added a test for goroutine counts"

CI summary: - unit: pass on all three SDKs - lint: one minor ts lint failure fixed in 7b9e21f - integration: flaky in first run due to staging KMS; re-run succeeded - smoke-staging: pass (new job verified behavior under 100 concurrent streams)

Backward compatibility and migration: No default behavior changed. The new APIs are opt-in under experimental namespaces for 2 releases; we will promote to GA after telemetry. Consumers who want built-in behavior can opt-in by calling the provided shims. Docs include migration examples from previous naive retry wrappers.

Telemetry and observability: Added telemetry flags (opt-in) that emit retry decisions and drop reasons to local debug logger by default and to structured traces when enabled. Follow-up work ENG-4837 will gate high-cardinality telemetry behind a feature flag.

Known limitations and follow-ups: - Server-side rate-limit collisions still need additional server signals; follow-up work tracked under ENG-4902. - We intentionally did not wire adaptive batching into the adapter; deferred to a separate change.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after approvals from Daniel and Marta. CI green at merge time.

Contact: Samira Cortez (author) — for follow-ups and rollout coordination.
